finding: SETTLED: a vetoing BeforeDropOrPaste (Cancel = True) SUPPRESSES a keyboard Ctrl+V paste. paste_veto rows: KeyDown(17=Ctrl, Shift=2) -> KeyDown(86=V, Shift=2) -> BeforeDropOrPaste(Cancel False->True; Action=2; data_object=present) -> KeyUp(86) -> KeyUp(17) -- NO Change fires and TextBox1.Value stays empty (the paste is suppressed). paste_baseline rows (no veto): KeyDown(17) -> KeyDown(86) -> BeforeDropOrPaste(Cancel False->False) -> Change(value=OxFormsPasteSeed) -> KeyUp(86) -> KeyUp(17) -- Change fires and the clipboard text is inserted. CONCLUSION (esq.17): honor the BeforeDropOrPaste Cancel=True veto by suppressing the paste (no text insert, no Change), analogous to the BeforeUpdate veto (esq.11). Because OxForms reduce_clipboard_result currently inserts BEFORE firing BeforeDropOrPaste, honoring the veto needs the insert DEFERRED until after the Cancel readback folds back (a two-stage paste). The Shift=2 (Ctrl) arg fidelity already landed in esq.13. A real Ctrl+V keystroke was used (KeyCode 17/86 are genuine VK codes, not VK_PACKET).
driving_method: Computer-use vision on a background-COM-hosted Excel running the committed w008-paste-veto fixture; the public Windows clipboard was seeded with "OxFormsPasteSeed", then a real Ctrl+V keystroke was sent. Each scenario was a separate ClearLog -> Show -> SetW008Scenario* -> drive -> export run, so the per-run sequence restarts at 1. The veto is armed by SetW008ScenarioPasteVeto (gVetoPaste True -> the handler sets Cancel.Value = True); the baseline leaves it False.
